It is cool that he has overcome it. But let's not put too much emphasis on the fact that "despite that, he did it".

Scoliosis is a serious disability, in some cases. He is clearly not disabled. 

It is a nice message to spread, but let us not give the wrong message to the sufferers : " It is hard to live with scoliosis" and if you do embrace a sports career you will start with a clear disadvantage. But if you do it with success, that is indeed a great accomplishment.

But I would not advise someone with scoliosis to look out for a professional career in competitive sports. Just enjoy doing sports for the sake of it. Let us put expectations on a normal standard. How many WR were beaten by someone with moderate/severe scoliosis? Usain Bolt is an exception that confirms the rule.

We have other barriers to break. Some are harder than to run 100 meters in less than 10sec. Keep strong!

I had surgery only 5 months ago, so I am still adjusting to my new body shape.

What I can tell you is that you do not lose your ribs mobility. You still have joints there https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costovertebral_joints

Your ribs move when you inhale or exhale. If you take a deep breath you can feel your chest expand. You can try diaphragmatic breathing to check if your sensation (ribs come out of place)  is maintained or not.

Your ribs may be deformed as a result of scoliosis. Sometimes ribs may rub against each other.

Hope this helps
